title: Cache Locally, Recompute Selectively for Streaming Video Understanding

problem.summary: Recent methods reduce query-time cost by prefilling frames into KV caches during idle time and reusing the cached KVs at query time.
statements: Recent methods reduce query-time cost by prefilling frames into KV caches during idle time and reusing the cached KVs at query time.
To bound per-frame computation over unbounded video streams, these methods restrict the context available during prefill.

This creates a fundamental context mismatch: the restricted context may omit information needed to properly contextualize video tokens, yet, still contain information irrelevant to the eventual query, which is unknown during prefill.

background.summary: Inspired by recomputation techniques in LLM serving (Yao et al., 2025; Hu et al., 2025), FrameBlend re-prefills a selected subset of tokens under the query-time context and overwrites their cached KVs.

evidence.quote: Inspired by recomputation techniques in LLM serving (Yao et al., 2025; Hu et al., 2025), FrameBlend re-prefills a selected subset of tokens under the query-time context and overwrites their cached KVs.

Together, shorter attention windows during idle-time prefill and query-time KV recomputation form the core principle of FrameBlend, improving both efficiency and accuracy without training, and with minimal modifications to existing SVU frameworks.

limitations.summary: We apply the short prefill window of FrameBlend by changing only this window size; the retrieval and decoding procedures remain unchanged.
items: We apply the short prefill window of FrameBlend by changing only this window size; the retrieval and decoding procedures remain unchanged.
At each layer, only frames that are both selected for recomputation and present in that layer's original retrieval set are replaced by their recomputed KVs.
FrameBlend uses sliding-window attention with a separate, small KV buffer, allowing each incoming token to attend only to the most recent tokens of the original stream within the prefill window.

At each layer, only frames that are both selected for recomputation and present in that layer's original retrieval set are replaced by their recomputed KVs.
For ReKV and LiveVLM, FrameBlend further reduces per-frame prefill FLOPs by 22.2-26.0% and prefill latency by 12.6-60.5% on RVS.
Even after accounting for query-time recomputation, total FLOPs and latency decrease by 19.0-23.2% and 14.1-58.7%, respectively.
